main_text.p: militudinem signi cum re significata, signo est impofita, Christo autore, nihil est aliud quã fundamēti ad suū terminum applicatio: quæ cùm magis proprie enunciari non possit, signum, hoc est fundamentum, nomen rei significatæ, tanquam sui termini, fortitur. Qui vnione sacramentalem malūt causam dicere ob quam panis Christi corpus vocetur: hi rectè quidē sentirēt, si eiusmodi coniunctionem ponerent qualis solet esse relatiuorū inter fese, & rerum ipsarum cum suis notis, siue verbis, siue visibilibus signis. Vt igitur vnaquæque vox, siue scriptilis, siue enuntiata, suam rem significatam, sibi adiunctam & inclusam continet: ita quoque sacramēta, vtpote verba visibilia, significãdo ea quæ diuina impositione & similitudine seu imagine quadam adumbrant, vnum quodammodo cum illis fiunt. Videntur autem isti realem & sub-stantialem magis quàm sacramen-talem vnionem ponere, quotquot

page.notes: The page is printed in roman type with some ligatures and long s, transcribed as plain s. The word "quotquot" closes the page and is the last full line. No catchword or signature is visible. Faint marks near the lower left of the text block appear to be show-through or noise and were not transcribed. Ambiguous readings: "signi cum" is printed with a space and is kept as printed; "fuũ" is read as "fuū" (tilde over u for m).
